discoveredAssets: http://localhost:3000/ - Homepage with navigation links - HTTP GET
http://localhost:3000/register - User registration endpoint - HTTP GET/POST
http://localhost:3000/login - User login endpoint - HTTP GET/POST
http://localhost:3000/profile/{userId} - User profile endpoint - HTTP GET/POST (IDOR risk)
http://localhost:3000/starttime - Application start timestamp - HTTP GET

targets.objective: Test registration endpoint for: password policy bypass, user enumeration, injection attacks (SQL/NoSQL), business logic flaws, mass assignment vulnerabilities, and analyze the 'distance' metric for weaknesses
targets.rationale: Registration endpoint accepts user input and returns JSON with internal application metrics including userId, userNumber, distance. POST endpoint is critical entry point requiring security testing for authentication and data validation flaws

targets.objective: Test login endpoint for: SQL injection, NoSQL injection, authentication bypass, brute force vulnerability, default credentials, password policy weaknesses, and session management flaws
targets.rationale: Authentication endpoint is critical security boundary. Form-based login with password field is potential vector for injection attacks and credential compromise. Redirects to profile on success.

targets.objective: Test for IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) vulnerability: access other users' profiles using different userId values, test both numeric IDs and MongoDB ObjectIds, test unauthorized access, enumerate valid userIds, test privilege escalation
targets.rationale: CRITICAL: Profile endpoint accepts userId in URL path with no visible authentication checks. Endpoint returns user profiles for any requested userId without validation. Primary attack surface for horizontal privilege escalation and user data disclosure.

targets.objective: Test session management: cookie handling, session fixation, privilege escalation via session manipulation, CSRF on profile modifications, and verify redirect behavior after login
targets.rationale: Login POST redirects to /profile/{userId} on success. Session token/cookie handling needs security review for proper session binding and CSRF protections

targets.objective: Test information disclosure: analyze revealed application metadata (start time, user count), test for timing attacks using this information, verify no other sensitive data leaked
targets.rationale: Endpoint reveals application start timestamp and user count without authentication. This timing information could be leveraged for side-channel attacks or understanding application deployment timing

targets.objective: Understand the 'distance' metric and 'target user' concept: analyze the hint system, identify application purpose, test for business logic flaws or race conditions in user registration, verify distance calculation algorithm
targets.rationale: Application appears to have a game/challenge mechanic with 'distance' and 'target user' elements. Understanding business logic is essential to identify manipulation opportunities, data leakage, or logic flaws

keyFindings: [CRITICAL] IDOR vulnerability likely exists on /profile/{userId} endpoint - accepts userId in URL without visible authentication checks
[CRITICAL] /profile/{userId} endpoint returned 200 OK for both valid and potentially invalid userIds - no validation observed
[HIGH] Registration endpoint (/register) returns application internal metrics including userId and userNumber - potential user enumeration vector
[HIGH] Login endpoint (/login) uses simple form-based authentication - prone to SQL/NoSQL injection attacks if not properly sanitized
[HIGH] No API documentation discovered - endpoints reverse-engineered through manual testing
[MEDIUM] Information disclosure on /info endpoint - reveals application start time (Unix timestamp) and total user count without authentication
[MEDIUM] Application appears to track user registration order with sequential userNumber - could enable user enumeration attacks
[MEDIUM] No robots.txt, sitemap.xml, or OpenAPI documentation found - suggests incomplete security configuration
[LOW] Application uses Express.js framework with jQuery 3.6.0 - technologies confirmed via X-Powered-By header and page source
